claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to ask: is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar), or on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education at the moment. He left school and isn't studying anything right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Since Alex is 17 and has left education, I have one more question: has Alex recently left education or training (within the past 20 weeks), or has he registered with a careers service, Connexions, or similar organisation as someone who is not in education, employment, or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or anything like that. He just left school and hasn't signed up with anyone.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Are you responsible for Alex and does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one more question:

Are you currently living in the UK, and do you have the right to live in the UK (for example, you're a British or Irish citizen, or have settled status, or have the right to work in the UK)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester. And yes, I have the right to live here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 17 years old
- He is not in full-time non-advanced education or approved training
- He has not registered with a careers service or similar organisation
- He left school more than 20 weeks ago (or at least hasn't maintained any connection with education/training services)

Unfortunately, Child Benefit typically stops when a child leaves full-time non-advanced education or approved training, unless they register with certain services. For children aged 16-19, eligibility generally continues only if they remain in qualifying education or training.

Let me provide you with the formal outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Reason:**
Alex is 17 years old and has left school. For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit can only continue if the child is:
- In full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, T-levels, NVQs up to level 3), or
- On an approved training course, or
- Has registered with a careers service or similar organisation after leaving education

Since Alex is not in qualifying education or training and hasn't registered with any careers service, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him at this time.

**What could change this?**
If Alex decides to return to full-time non-advanced education or start an approved training course before he turns 20, you may become eligible again. Alternatively, if he registers with a careers service, there may be a short extension period available.

Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify?

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and has left school. He is not currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or equivalent) and is not on an approved training course. For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit eligibility continues only if the child remains in qualifying full-time non-advanced education or approved training, or if they have left but registered with an appropriate careers or support service. Since Alex does not meet any of these criteria, the claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for him.
